# PEN-3713 — pin the GitHub egress wrappers to the front of the agent Job's PATH

`src/server/job-manifest.ts`, in `buildEnvVars()`: after the four env layers
collapse into `merged`, prepend `/usr/local/libexec/paperclip/bin` — the
root-owned directory the image now installs the GitHub egress wrappers into —
to `merged.PATH`, idempotently.

Why the adapter and not the chart. `paperclip.runtimePath` already fails the
Helm render when a wrapper directory is missing from PATH or lands after
`/usr/bin`, but that guard only renders onto the StatefulSet and the api
Deployment. An agent Job's PATH comes from layer 3 (`selfPod.inheritedEnv`) or
layer 4 (`adapterConfig.env.PATH`, an operator-set database value), and layer 4
is a flat last-writer-wins assignment with no shape check on any key. So the
invariant was enforced everywhere except the containers that actually run
agents.

Measured on a live agent pod 2026-10-02: `PATH` began
`/paperclip/opencode-api-key-bin:/paperclip/bin:…` and did not contain the
wrapper directory at all, so `git` resolved to `/usr/bin/git` and PEN-3156's
wrapper was off the traffic path — while the chart's render guard reported
healthy.

**That measurement is from a `claude_k8s` pod, and this change does reach it.**
An earlier revision of this file asserted the opposite — that the leading
`/paperclip/opencode-api-key-bin` made the pod an `opencode_k8s` agent, placing
it outside this commit's reach. That was wrong, and re-measured 2026-10-03
(PEN-3732) it is wrong in the direction that understates the fix:

- The identical PATH string was reproduced on a pod labelled
  `paperclip.io/adapter-type=claude_k8s`, container `claude`, image
  `paperclip-agent:sha-4e00ff2-k8s-vendored`. The directory is therefore not
  opencode-specific.
- It arrives at **layer 4**, not layer 3. The chart's default runtime PATH is
  `<mountPath>/.local/bin:<mountPath>/bin:…` (`_helpers.tpl`), and
  `values.blockcast.yaml` sets no `env.path` override, so the server pod's PATH
  — the layer-3 source — cannot be where it comes from; the string
  `opencode-api-key-bin` does not appear anywhere in this repository. The
  observed value is the chart default with `/paperclip/.local/bin` *swapped for*
  `/paperclip/opencode-api-key-bin`, carried by `adapterConfig.env.PATH`.
- Neither vendored adapter constructs PATH at all. `claude_k8s`
  (`0.2.6-blockcast.11`) and `opencode_k8s` (`0.2.6`) both merely allowlist
  `PATH` for inheritance, and both end their merge with `adapterConfig.env` on a
  last-writer-wins assignment.
- The shell PATH read above is the manifest PATH, not a profile-modified one:
  `/paperclip/.profile`, `.bashrc` and `.zshenv` each prepend
  `$HOME/.local/bin` when absent, and `/paperclip/.local/bin` is absent from it.

So the half this commit does not reach is `opencode_k8s` *as a code path*, not
as the population behind the evidence. Two consequences for the follow-up:

- **The mirror change may not be needed to fix the PATH.** Because
  `adapterConfig.env.PATH` is layer 4 and last-writer-wins in the opencode
  adapter too, correcting that database value gives an opencode Job the right
  ordering with no fork change and no `OPENCODE_K8S_REF` bump. A fork change is
  the right durable fix — config is not a security control — but it is not the
  only route, and it is not on the critical path.
- **The opencode adapter's source is readable**, at
  `/opt/paperclip-bundled-adapters/node_modules/paperclip-adapter-opencode-k8s`
  inside the agent image. The earlier "which env layer it assembles PATH from
  has not been read" no longer holds; it is the four-layer merge described above.

Not verified: the literal bytes of `adapterConfig.env.PATH` (the API redacts the
value; the layer is inferred from the live PATH plus the absence of any chart
override), and whether opencode agents outside this cluster carry the same
override. This cluster ran **no** `opencode_k8s` workloads at all **as measured
2026-10-03** — 0 pods and 0 Jobs carrying that adapter label, against positive
controls of 27 pods and 30 Jobs for `claude_k8s`. That is a point-in-time
census, not a standing property: it cannot see a workload that ran between two
observations, and the gap it stands down re-opens silently if opencode is
re-enabled, with the render guard green throughout. PEN-3732 owns the
substantive `opencode_k8s` PATH gap; re-measure before relying on this sentence.

Prepend rather than reject: a malformed operator PATH is a misconfiguration
that would otherwise fail Jobs with nothing to do with GitHub, and the property
worth guaranteeing here is the ordering. When no PATH is present at all the
system default is used as the base, because emitting a lone directory would
clobber the image's own `ENV PATH` and leave nothing else resolvable. Leaving
`PATH` unset entirely in that case would preserve the image's own toolchain
entries, but it is the one case where nothing else enforces the ordering, so the
wrapper directory would be absent rather than merely late.
